thread:
Maya (Support): Hey folks — customer ACME reported sudden logouts across several web apps after our maintenance at 03:10 UTC. Ticket CS-5021. They're seeing 401s with `invalid_session` and a console message: "device_tkn decrypt failed".

Anna (CSE): Seen similar from a telecom customer — only web clients on Chrome get booted, native mobile apps still ok. They mentioned they did not clear cookies.

session-bot: Detected spike: 2025-11-02T03:12:10Z — 401s from /v1/session/validate for cookie_version=3, user_agent like "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows)".

Maya (Support): Repro steps from ACME: 1) Login on browser, 2) wait ~30s, 3) call API with Authorization cookie, 4) return 401. They attached network log.

Eli (Eng): Thanks. I'm looking at the session service logs around the rotation window. Quick check: did we rotate the KMS key or bump cookie encryption version as part of the maintenance? @Sam?

Sam (SRE): We rotated the kms alias for sesh-encrypt yesterday, and a tiny deploy added cookie_version=3 that expects an envelope format with 'kid' present. I see some sessions issued with cookie_version=2 still live.

Eli (Eng): That could be it — if the browser cookie bundle lacks the new 'kid' envelope, our decrypt path returns ErrUnsupportedCipher and we kick users. Mobile SDK had a fallback path for legacy cookies which is why native apps are fine. Web runtime didn't get fallback.

Anna (CSE): Customer says affected users did NOT re-auth; they were mid-session. We need a mitigation that doesn't force re-login for 10k users.

Maya (Support): Customer wants temporary fix or a way to reissue sessions without asking users to log in. Any ETA?

Eli (Eng): Immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll back cookie_version enforcement — allow decrypt with legacy key if kid missing (fast but risky). 2) Add a short-lived compatibility key in KMS and re-decrypt old cookies server-side then reissue version=3 cookie via a silent endpoint. 3) Ask customers to clear cookies (bad UX).

Sam (SRE): Rollback is quickest. I can patch the runtime to accept old envelope format within 30min and redeploy canary to us-east-1. That will reduce surface and avoid mass re-login.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by Sam: staging -> canary -> global. Change id: deploy-20251102-ky1.

Eli (Eng): Before we rollback I want to confirm attack vectors. If we accept legacy format, we must ensure we still verify HMAC and token expiry to avoid session fixation.

Maya (Support): Customer update: they see intermittent 401s on admin routes, page reloads sometimes fix it for a bit. They are getting nervous.

Sam (SRE): Rolling back cookie_version enforcement now to canary. I'll patch flag `cookie.enforce_version = false`.

Eli (Eng): Also creating a one-off endpoint to reissue session cookies for a user list: POST /admin/sessions/reissue { "user_ids": [...] } which will: load cookie, decrypt with legacy key, generate new envelope with kid and set cookie_version=3. Use only with audit.

Anna (CSE): Please add audit log and rate-limit the endpoint — we will coordinate with ACME to provide a list of active users (they have ~120 affected). Anna -> Maya: ask them for sample user ids and web session cookies.

Maya (Support): Sent ACME the instructions to export session cookies and user ids. They're uploading a CSV.

Eli (Eng): Logs showing example error snippet:

```
error=decrypt_failed reason=unsupported_cipher cookie_id=abc123 user=alice@example.com svc=session-svc env=prod
stack=github.com/redwood/sessions.decrypt: ErrUnsupportedCipher
```

Eli (Eng): And the offending header example from network capture:

```
Cookie: rw_session=eyJ2IjoxLCJkYXRhIjoi... (no kid field)
X-Forwarded-Host: app.acme.local
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)
```

Sam (SRE): Canary patch applied to prod-us-east at 03:45 UTC. Error rate for invalid_session dropped by ~86% in that region. Rolling to global now.

deploy-bot: Canary succeeded. Promoting to global in 5m.

Maya (Support): Passing update to ACME: we applied a hotfix to accept legacy cookies while we schedule reissue. They're relieved.

Anna (CSE): Next steps: 1) Run reissue endpoint for ACME's CSV once we have auditing in place. 2) Add migration job that automatically reissues cookies on next valid request. 3) Postmortem to explain KMS rotation + cookie versioning gap.

Eli (Eng): I'll own the reissue endpoint and the migration job. Sam — please make sure the KMS alias rotates with a backwards-compatibility plan next time (create a deprecation window and feature flag).

Sam (SRE): Agreed. Also adding a smoke test that logs in with older SDKs and validates cookies after key rotations.

Maya (Support): ACME uploaded CSV. Ticket updated with our mitigation plan and ETA: reissue run in 2 hours with audit.

Anna (CSE): Thank you team. I'll follow up with ACME post-migration.

Eli (Eng): Filing INC-7890 to track the incident and postmortem. Will include timeline, root cause, and remediation.

Maya (Support): Closing loop here for now. Will add final customer message after reissue. :thumbsup:
